exposure: family socioeconomic status (Multidimensional Poverty Index, parental education)
cohort: The study included mothers from sub-Saharan Africa who had at least three children, identifying families with children having confirmed sickle cell anaemia (cases) and control families with children without the disease from the same area.
finding: Mortality rates were 15.3% for children with sickle cell anaemia younger than 1 year, 36.4% younger than 5 years, and 43.3% younger than 10 years, with belonging to a family with sickle cell anaemia independently increasing the risk of mortality.
country: Burkina Faso, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Mali, Senegal
